instructions:
Each item is an ontology term that a column of sample metadata in a gene
expression study can mean. Write up to 5 aliases for each term: other ways a
researcher would write that same variable as a column header in sample
metadata.

Good aliases:
- common abbreviations and acronyms ("sbp" for systolic blood pressure)
- shorter everyday phrasings ("systolic bp", "visual acuity")
- the plain name of the quantity when the term's label is wordy
  ("intraocular pressure" for "intraocular pressure measurement")

Rules:
- An alias must mean the same variable as the term: not a broader or narrower
  one, and not a related one.
- No values ("male", "high"), units on their own, gene or tool names, or
  dataset-specific codes.
- No alias that only rewords the label trivially (plural, case,
  punctuation). Those are matched already.
- Fewer is better than wrong. If a term has no natural alias, return an empty
  list.

Examples:
- systolic blood pressure -> ["sbp", "systolic bp", "systolic pressure"]
- intraocular pressure measurement -> ["intraocular pressure", "iop"]
- visual acuity measurement -> ["visual acuity", "va"]

items.label: family history of diabetes
items.definition: A reported family history of diabetes in one or more family members.

items.label: family history of heart disease
items.definition: A reported family history of heart disease in one or more family members.

items.label: family history of high blood pressure
items.definition: A reported family history of high blood pressure in one or more family members.

items.label: menstrual symptom severity
items.definition: A measurement assessing the severity of symptoms experienced during menstruation, including but not limited to pain, cramping, discomfort, and other physical or psychological manifestations that may affect quality of life.

items.label: visceral adiposity index
items.definition: A sex-specific mathematical index calculated from body mass index, waist circumference, triglycerides, and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol that estimates visceral adipose tissue function and serves as an indicator of adipose tissue dysfunction and cardiometabolic risk.

items.label: BMI-adjusted visceral adiposity index
items.definition: A visceral adiposity index value that has been statistically adjusted for body mass index to account for overall adiposity, allowing assessment of visceral adipose tissue dysfunction independent of general obesity status.

items.label: body adiposity index
items.definition: A calculated anthropometric index derived from hip circumference and height using the formula ((hip circumference in cm) / (height in m)^1.5) - 18, which directly estimates percent body fat for adult men and women without requiring body weight measurement.

items.label: BMI-adjusted body adiposity index
items.definition: A body adiposity index value that has been statistically adjusted for body mass index, enabling the assessment of the relationship between hip circumference-derived adiposity and health outcomes independent of overall body weight status.

items.label: imaging protocol
items.definition: A protocol which provides instructions on the process of creating visual representations of specimens or phenomena.

items.label: fixation protocol
items.definition: A protocol that specifies the steps and conditions for fixation of biological material (e.g. cells or tissues), using chemical and/or physical methods to preserve structural and molecular features and limit post-collection degradation (including autolysis/putrefaction) for downstream analysis.

items.label: permeabilization time
items.definition: A measurement of the duration for which cells or cell membranes are kept in a permeabilized state to enable increased transmembrane passage of otherwise poorly permeant molecules (for example, dyes, antibodies, or nucleic acids).

items.label: sample ID
items.definition: A string used to identify a sample.

items.label: myocardial strain
items.definition: Myocardial strain refers to the measurement of heart muscle deformation, or its shortening, thickening, and lengthening, using imaging techniques like echocardiography.

items.label: biparietal distance
items.definition: A measurement of the distance spanning the widest transverse diameter of the fetal skull, between the outer or inner tables of the two parietal bones, typically obtained by ultrasound.

items.label: amniotic fluid index
items.definition: A semi-quantitative prenatal ultrasound measurement of amniotic fluid volume, calculated as the sum of the deepest vertical pocket of amniotic fluid measured in each of the four quadrants of the uterus.

items.label: fetal heart rate
items.definition: The rate of contraction of the fetal heart, typically expressed as the number of fetal cardiac beats per minute.

items.label: MPLEx
items.definition: An extraction protocol that partitions a single biological sample into metabolite, protein, and lipid fractions for subsequent multi-omics analyses, typically using mass spectrometry.

items.label: apnea-hypopnea index measurement
items.definition: A measurement of sleep apnea severity calculated as the total number of apnea and hypopnea events recorded during a sleep study, divided by the total number of hours of sleep.

items.label: cigarette smoking status measurement
items.definition: A self-reported categorical measurement of an individual's cigarette smoking history, classified as current smoker, former smoker, or never smoker.

items.label: slide ID
items.definition: A unique identifier for the physical glass slide or cartridge on which a tissue section is mounted and processed.

items.label: Atrophy
items.definition: Any weakening or degeneration, especially through lack of use.

items.label: rheumatic fever nodule
items.definition: A small round or oval, mostly subcutaneous nodule made up chiefly of a mass of Aschoff bodies and seen in cases of rheumatic fever. It is differentiated from the RHEUMATOID NODULE which appears in rheumatoid arthritis, most frequently over bony prominences. (From Dorland, 27th ed)

items.label: Skull Fractures
items.definition: Fractures of the skull which may result from penetrating or nonpenetrating head injuries or rarely BONE DISEASES (see also FRACTURES, SPONTANEOUS). items.label: Eye Burns
items.definition: Injury to any part of the eye by extreme heat, chemical agents, or ultraviolet radiation.

items.label: Periprosthetic Fractures
items.definition: Fractures around joint replacement prosthetics or implants. They can occur intraoperatively or postoperatively.

items.label: disease
items.definition: A disease is a disposition to undergo pathological processes that exists in an organism because of one or more disorders in that organism.

items.label: ischemia reperfusion injury
items.definition: Adverse functional, metabolic, or structural changes in ischemic tissues resulting from the restoration of blood flow to the tissue (reperfusion), including swelling; hemorrhage; necrosis; and damage from free radicals. The most common instance is myocardial reperfusion injury.

items.label: spinal fracture
items.definition: Traumatic or pathological injury to the spine in which the continuity of a vertebral bone is broken. Symptoms include back pain and difficulty bending and twisting.

items.label: bone fracture
items.definition: Breaks in bones.

items.label: humerus fracture
items.definition: A traumatic or pathologic injury to the humerus in which the continuity of the humerus is broken.

items.label: tibia fracture
items.definition: Traumatic or pathological injury to the tibia in which the continuity of the bone is broken.

items.label: ulna fracture
items.definition: Fractures of the larger bone of the forearm.

items.label: radius fracture
items.definition: Traumatic or pathological injury to the radius bone in which the continuity of the bone is broken.

items.label: hip fracture
items.definition: Traumatic or pathological injury to the hip in which the continuity of either the femoral head, femoral neck, intertrochanteric or subtrochanteric regions is broken. items.label: inherited disease susceptibility
items.definition: A latent susceptibility to disease at the genetic level, which may be activated under certain conditions.

items.label: disease characteristic
items.definition: An attribute of a disease.

items.label: syndromic or isolated
items.definition: An characteristic of a disease that varies depending on whether the disease appears as an isolated feature or whether the disease is a syndrome consisting of multiple features.

items.label: has a syndromic presentation
items.definition: An characteristic of a disease in which the disease is not manifested as an isolated feature but has multiple distinct features.

items.label: has an isolated presentation
items.definition: An characteristic of a disease in which the disease is manifested as an isolated feature.

items.label: congenital
items.definition: A characteristic of a disease in which the disease is present at birth, regardless of cause.

items.label: inherited
items.definition: A characteristic of a disease in which the cause of the disease is a genetic problem inherited from either or both parents.

items.label: injury
items.definition: Damage inflicted on the body as the direct or indirect result of an external force, with or without disruption of structural continuity.

items.label: tumor grading characteristic
items.definition: A modifier that can be applied to a tumor class describing abnormal tumor histology or morphology. It is an indicator of how quickly a tumor is likely to grow and spread

items.label: general tumor grading characteristic
items.definition: A term that refers to the cellular differentiation of a malignant cellular infiltrate. A cancer is defined through grades I-IV (or 1-4), or as well, moderately, poorly differentiated or undifferentiated.

items.label: spinal injury
items.definition: A injury that involves the vertebral column.

items.label: disease susceptibility
items.definition: A constitution or condition of the body which makes the tissues react in special ways to certain extrinsic stimuli and thus tends to make the individual more than usually susceptible to certain diseases.

items.label: radiation injury
items.definition: Harmful effects of non-experimental exposure to ionizing or non-ionizing radiation in VERTEBRATES.

items.label: opportunistic infectious
items.definition: A characteristic of an infectious disease in which the disease affects an immunologically compromised host.

items.label: primary infectious
items.definition: A characteristic of an infectious disease in which the disease affects an immunologically normal host.

items.label: jaw fracture
items.definition: A traumatic or pathologic injury to the jaw in which the continuity of the bone is broken.

items.label: classic or non-classic genetic disease presentation
items.definition: A classic (severe) or non-classic (mild or intermediate) form of a genetic disease.

items.label: classic presentation
items.definition: A severe form of a genetic disease.

items.label: non-classic presentation
items.definition: A mild or intermediate form of a genetic disease.

items.label: iatrogenic or non-iatrogenic
items.definition: A iatrogenic or non-iatrogenic form of a disease.

items.label: iatrogenic
items.definition: A characteristic of a diseae which results from diagnostic and therapeutic procedures undertaken on a patient.

items.label: non-iatrogenic
items.definition: A characteristic of a diseae in which it does not result from diagnostic and therapeutic procedures undertaken on a patient.

items.label: idiopathic vs non-idiopathic
items.definition: A disease characteristic in which the cause of the disease is known or unknown.

items.label: idiopathic
items.definition: A disease characteristic in which the disease has an uncertain or unknown cause.

items.label: non-idiopathic
items.definition: A disease characteristic in which the disease has a known cause.

items.label: mosaic vs complete
items.definition: A disease characteristic in which the cause of the disease is present in some of the cells of the organism, or in all the cells of the organism.

items.label: mosaic
items.definition: A disease characteristic in which the cause of the disease is present in some of the cells of the organism.

items.label: complete
items.definition: A disease characteristic in which the cause of the disease is present in all the cells of the organism.

items.label: material supplier role
items.definition: a role realized through the process of supplying materials such as animal subjects, reagents or other materials used in an investigation.

items.label: mass spectrometer

items.label: investigation
items.definition: a planned process that consists of parts: planning, study design execution, documentation and which produce conclusion(s).

items.label: assay
items.definition: An assay is a process with the objective to create as an output information about a material entity (bearing evaluant role).

items.label: quantitative confidence value
items.definition: A data item which is used to indicate the degree of uncertainty about a measurement.

items.label: gene list
items.definition: A gene list is a report of the names or identifiers of genes that are the outcome of an analysis or have been put together for the purpose of an analysis.

items.label: population
items.definition: a population is a collection of individuals from the same taxonomic class living, counted or sampled at a particular site or in a particular area

items.label: imaging assay
items.definition: An assay that produces a picture of an entity.

items.label: organization
items.definition: An organization is a continuant entity which can play roles,  has members, and has a set of organization rules. items.label: protocol
items.definition: a protocol is a plan specification which has sufficient level of detail and quantitative information to communicate it between domain experts, so that different domain experts will reliably be able to independently reproduce the process.

items.label: analyte role
items.definition: A measurand role borne by a molecular entity or an atom and realized in an analyte assay which achieves the objective to measure the magnitude/concentration/amount of the analyte in the entity bearing evaluant role.

items.label: polymerase chain reaction
items.definition: PCR is the process in which a DNA polymerase is used to amplify a piece of DNA by in vitro enzymatic replication. As PCR progresses, the DNA thus generated is itself used as a template for replication. This sets in motion a chain reaction in which the DNA template is exponentially amplified.

items.label: enzyme
items.definition: (protein or rna) or has_part (protein or rna) and has_function some GO:0003824 (catalytic activity)

items.label: single cell isolation
items.definition: a process in which a population of cells with certain characteristics is isolated from a larger population

items.label: isolation of adherent cells
items.definition: a material separation process in which cells that stick to the container in which they are grown as a cell culture are separated from those in the liquid component of the culture. The output of this process are adherent cells.

items.label: reverse transcribed polymerase chain reaction
items.definition: reverse transcribe pcr is a process which allow amplification of cDNA during a pcr reaction while the cDNA results from a retrotranscription of messenger RNA isolated from a material entity.

items.label: differential expression analysis data transformation
items.definition: A differential expression analysis data transformation is a data transformation that has objective differential expression analysis

items.label: specimen collection process
items.definition: A planned process with the objective to obtain a material entity for potential use as an input upon which measurements or observations are performed.

items.label: Helicos sequencing assay
items.definition: Helicos sequencing is a DNA sequencing which allows sequence identification of billions of DNA molecules immobilized to a surface by using DNA polymerase and fluorescently labeled nucleotides added one at a time. items.label: library preparation
items.definition: process which results in the creation of a library from fragments of DNA using cloning vectors or oligonucleotides with the role of adaptors

items.label: Solexa sequencing assay

items.label: material sample
items.definition: A material which is collected with the intention of being representative of a greater whole (i.e. a sample).

items.label: study design independent variable
items.definition: a directive information entity that is part of a study design. items.label: study design controlled variable
items.definition: Controlled variable specification is a part of a study design. They are the entities that could vary, but are kept constant to prevent their influence on the effect of the independent variable on the dependent.

items.label: polyA RNA extract
items.definition: A RNA extract that is the output of an extraction process in which RNA molecules with poly A tail at its 3’ end are purified.

items.label: frozen specimen
items.definition: A specimen that has been frozen in order to store it.

items.label: labeled specimen
items.definition: A specimen  that has been modified in order to be able to detect it in future experiments.
